pairs.why: A keeps broad soft shapes with few thin lines, while B adds many fine rigging lines, plank scoring and busy wave edges that the real ship's soft, chunky linework lacks.

A's thick, soft-edged door frame and dense leaf edges match the real door's chunky contours and busy ivy better than B's thin hinge lines and sparse, crisp planks.
B's body edges are softer and its rivets less crisp, closer to the real duck's smooth, sparse linework.

A has soft, clean boundaries and lower edge density, while B has fine rigging threads, hull grain scoring and busy water, which the real ship's smooth edges lack.
